title: Reporting Defects & Roadworthiness
whatItIs: You're legally responsible for your vehicle's condition on the road. Record every defect from your walkaround check or journey in writing and report it to the person who sorts out defects.

keyFacts.text: Drivers MUST report any defects, or symptoms of defects, that could prevent the vehicle being operated safely.
You MUST get dangerous defects fixed before you continue your journey.

keyFacts: On a tachograph, record the walkaround check and any repairs as 'other work'.

items.title: Check
items.text: At least once in every 24 hours the vehicle is used.

items.title: Record
items.text: Registration, date, defects or 'nil', your name.

items.title: Report
items.text: In writing, to the person who sorts out defects.

items.title: Act
items.text: The vehicle may be taken out of service.

items.title: Repair and keep
items.text: Defect reports are kept for at least 15 months.

a.label: 'S' marked prohibition
points: Should have been found, e.g. at the daily check

b.label: 'X' marked defect
points: Random failure the driver wouldn't notice
No reflection on the maintenance system

onTheTest.question: You find no defects during your walkaround check. What should you record?
onTheTest.why: Record 'nil' defects if you don't find any: it shows the check was done and no defects were found.

onTheTest.question: On your journey you notice a dangerous defect. What must you do?
options: Finish the day and report it at the depot
Stop safely, report it and get it fixed before going on
Report it at tomorrow's walkaround check
Drive on slowly with hazard lights on
onTheTest.why: Stop somewhere safe to assess and report it. Dangerous defects must be fixed before you continue.

traps: Someone else did the check? You still need to see evidence it was done.
Not doing an adequate walkaround check can lead to a driver conduct hearing and loss of your vocational licence.
Using an HGV in a dangerous condition can mean an unlimited fine and a prison sentence.
